note: 4.1.1 Parsing was removed in WCAG 2.2. AAA criteria are included only where they inform enhanced targets.

criteria.title: Non-text Content
criteria.description: All non-text content has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose.

criteria.title: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
criteria.description: Prerecorded audio-only and video-only media have an alternative that presents equivalent information.

criteria.title: Captions (Prerecorded)
criteria.description: Captions are provided for all prerecorded audio content in synchronized media.

criteria.title: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
criteria.description: An alternative for time-based media or audio description is provided for prerecorded video content.

criteria.title: Captions (Live)
criteria.description: Captions are provided for all live audio content in synchronized media.

criteria.title: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
criteria.description: Audio description is provided for all prerecorded video content in synchronized media.

criteria.title: Info and Relationships
criteria.description: Information, structure, and relationships conveyed through presentation are programmatically determinable or available in text.

criteria.title: Meaningful Sequence
criteria.description: When the sequence in which content is presented affects its meaning, a correct reading sequence is programmatically determinable.

criteria.title: Sensory Characteristics
criteria.description: Instructions for understanding and operating content do not rely solely on sensory characteristics such as shape, color, size, location, or sound.

criteria.title: Orientation
criteria.description: Content does not restrict its display and operation to a single display orientation unless essential.

criteria.title: Identify Input Purpose
criteria.description: The purpose of each input field collecting information about the user can be programmatically determined.

criteria.title: Use of Color
criteria.description: Color is not used as the only visual means of conveying information, indicating an action, prompting a response, or distinguishing a visual element.

criteria.title: Audio Control
criteria.description: If audio plays automatically for more than 3 seconds, a mechanism is available to pause or stop it, or to control volume independently.

criteria.title: Contrast (Minimum)
criteria.description: Text and images of text have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, except large text and incidental text.

criteria.title: Resize Text
criteria.description: Text can be resized without assistive technology up to 200 percent without loss of content or functionality.

criteria.title: Images of Text
criteria.description: Images of text are used only when the particular presentation is essential or the image can be customized.

criteria.title: Contrast (Enhanced)
criteria.description: Text has a contrast ratio of at least 7:1; large text at least 4.5:1.

criteria.title: Reflow
criteria.description: Content can be presented without loss of information or functionality, and without requiring scrolling in two dimensions at 320 CSS pixels.

criteria.title: Non-text Contrast
criteria.description: Visual information required to identify UI components and states, and graphical objects, has a contrast ratio of at least 3:1.

criteria.title: Text Spacing
criteria.description: No loss of content or functionality occurs when text spacing is increased to specified values.

criteria.title: Content on Hover or Focus
criteria.description: Additional content on hover or focus is dismissible, hoverable, and persistent.

criteria.title: Keyboard
criteria.description: All functionality is operable through a keyboard interface.

criteria.title: No Keyboard Trap
criteria.description: Keyboard focus is never trapped; focus can be moved away using standard keyboard interfaces.

criteria.title: Character Key Shortcuts
criteria.description: Single-character shortcuts can be turned off, remapped, or activated only on focus.

criteria.title: Timing Adjustable
criteria.description: Time limits can be extended, adjusted, or turned off.

criteria.title: Pause, Stop, Hide
criteria.description: Moving, blinking, scrolling, or auto-updating content can be paused, stopped, or hidden.

criteria.title: Timeouts
criteria.description: Users are informed of timeouts and can extend or cancel them.

criteria.title: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
criteria.description: Content does not flash more than three times in any one-second period.

criteria.title: Animation from Interactions
criteria.description: Motion animation triggered by interaction can be disabled unless essential.

criteria.title: Bypass Blocks
criteria.description: A mechanism is available to skip repeated blocks of content.

criteria.title: Page Titled
criteria.description: Web pages have titles that describe topic or purpose.

criteria.title: Focus Order
criteria.description: A logical focus order preserves meaning and operability.

criteria.title: Link Purpose (In Context)
criteria.description: The purpose of each link can be determined from the link text or its context.

criteria.title: Multiple Ways
criteria.description: More than one way is available to locate a web page within a set of web pages.

criteria.title: Headings and Labels
criteria.description: Headings and labels describe topic or purpose.

criteria.title: Focus Visible
criteria.description: Any keyboard-operable user interface has a visible focus indicator.

criteria.title: Location
criteria.description: The user is informed about their location within a set of web pages.

criteria.title: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
criteria.description: When a component receives keyboard focus, it is not entirely hidden by author-created content.

criteria.title: Pointer Gestures
criteria.description: Multipoint or path-based gestures have a single-pointer alternative unless essential.

criteria.title: Pointer Cancellation
criteria.description: Pointer activation can be cancelled or undone.

criteria.title: Label in Name
criteria.description: The accessible name contains the visible label text.

criteria.title: Motion Actuation
criteria.description: Functionality triggered by device motion has an alternative and can be disabled.

criteria.title: Dragging Movements
criteria.description: Dragging movements have a single-pointer alternative unless essential.

criteria.title: Target Size (Minimum) (2.2)
criteria.description: Pointer targets meet the 24 by 24 CSS pixel minimum or spacing exception.

criteria.title: Language of Page
criteria.description: The default human language of each web page can be programmatically determined.

criteria.title: Language of Parts
criteria.description: The human language of each passage or phrase can be programmatically determined.

criteria.title: On Focus
criteria.description: Receiving focus does not initiate a change of context.

criteria.title: On Input
criteria.description: Changing a setting does not automatically change context unless the user is advised.

criteria.title: Consistent Navigation
criteria.description: Repeated navigation mechanisms occur in the same relative order.

criteria.title: Consistent Identification
criteria.description: Components with the same functionality are identified consistently.

criteria.title: Consistent Help
criteria.description: Help mechanisms occur in the same relative order across pages.

criteria.title: Error Identification
criteria.description: Input errors are identified in text and described to the user.

criteria.title: Labels or Instructions
criteria.description: Labels or instructions are provided when content requires user input.

criteria.title: Error Suggestion
criteria.description: Suggestions for correcting input errors are provided in text.

criteria.title: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
criteria.description: Users can review, confirm, and reverse submissions for legal, financial, or data transactions.

criteria.title: Redundant Entry
criteria.description: Information previously entered is not required to be re-entered in the same process.

criteria.title: Accessible Authentication
criteria.description: Authentication does not rely on a cognitive function test, and users can passkey, paste, or use a password manager.

criteria.title: Accessible Authentication (Enhanced)
criteria.description: Authentication requires no cognitive function test.

criteria.title: Name, Role, Value
criteria.description: For all UI components, name, role, and value can be programmatically determined and are exposed to assistive technologies.

criteria.title: Status Messages
criteria.description: Status messages are exposed through roles and properties so assistive technologies can announce them without receiving focus.
